answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The tundra multiplier is published, charged in juniper, and thread lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3102 identities would post 4421 proofs and burn roughly 74 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
